name: message
title: Message
description: One thing somebody said, and where it stands with the screen. Five moderation states on one attribute, `data-gs-moderation`: sending, screening, published, held and refused. Every one of them is host-declared, published included, because TalkBox does the screening and this draws whatever comes back, the same seam the cue runtime uses for sound. Four speakers on `data-gs-author`: you, another player, the host and the room itself, which has no name and no avatar because nobody owns it. A refused message is struck through, marked with a cross and left on screen, which is three changes at once rather than a colour. The words are rendered as text and never as markup. Decides nothing: it does not screen, does not hide and does not hold a clock, so the timestamp arrives already formatted.
docs: Pass `moderation` on every message; the default is `published` and the component never changes it. `screening` and `refused` are author-only states: a host sends them to the person who wrote the message and to nobody else, because nobody else ever received it. This component will draw whatever it is given, so hiding another player's refused message is the host's job and not a prop. Pass `time` already formatted, in the player's locale, once the message is published; before that the status line has something to say instead and the time is not drawn. `author="system"` renders the centred, unowned line a room uses for its own announcements: give it no `name` and no `avatar`. `pinned` marks the host message a stream holds at its top; it changes the marker, not the placing, which belongs to `chat-stream`.
